examples.ko: 결혼반지를 사러 금은방에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the jewelry shop to buy wedding rings.

examples.ko: 동네 금은방에서 시계 줄을 고쳤어요.
examples.en: I got my watch strap fixed at the neighborhood jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 금은방 사장님이 반지 크기를 재 주셨어요.
examples.en: The jewelry shop owner measured my ring size.

examples.ko: 할머니가 금은방에서 돌 반지를 맞춰 오셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother had a first-birthday ring made at the jewelry shop.

examples.ko: 금은방 앞을 지나다가 예쁜 목걸이를 봤어요.
examples.en: Passing in front of a jewelry shop, I saw a pretty necklace.

examples.ko: 요즘은 금은방보다 온라인에서 액세서리를 사는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days more people buy accessories online than at jewelry shops.

explain: 금과 은으로 만든 장신구를 파는 동네 가게예요. 반지, 목걸이를 사거나 금을 팔 때 가는 곳이고, 백화점 매장은 보통 '귀금속 매장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I picked out a necklace at the jewelry shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 가게를 가리키는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal word for the same kind of shop.

phrases.en: I sold my unused gold ring to a jewelry store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금을 팔러 갈 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common expression when selling gold.
phrases.en_equiv: to sell to a jewelry store

phrases.en: The jewelry store owner polished the ring for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동네 가게의 주인을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the owner of a neighborhood shop.

explain_en: It is a small neighborhood shop selling gold and silver jewelry. People go there to buy rings and necklaces or to sell gold, while a department store counter is usually called '귀금속 매장'.

examples.ko: 학교는 형편이 어려운 학생에게 급식비를 보조해요.
examples.en: The school helps students in difficult circumstances with their meal fees.

examples.ko: 급식비는 매달 말일까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: The school meal fee must be paid by the end of each month.

examples.ko: 이번 달 급식비가 얼마인지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how much the school meal fee is this month.

examples.ko: 급식비를 못 낸 학생은 선생님께 말씀드리세요.
examples.en: Students who couldn't pay the meal fee should tell the teacher.

examples.ko: 형제가 둘이면 급식비가 두 배로 들어요.
examples.en: With two siblings, the meal fees cost double.

examples.ko: 동생 급식비를 자동이체로 신청했어요.
examples.en: I signed up for automatic payment of my sibling's school meal fee.

explain: 학교에서 먹는 점심 같은 단체 급식에 내는 돈이에요. 학교 공지문이나 가정통신문에 자주 나오고, 집에서 쓰는 식비와는 구분해요.

phrases.en: I paid this month's school meal fee.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you paid the meal fee.
phrases.en_equiv: to pay the school meal fee

phrases.en: I applied for school meal fee support.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in school notices.

phrases.en: How much is the school meal fee per month?
phrases.nuance_ko: 금액을 물어볼 때 쓰는 쉬운 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple question for asking the amount.
phrases.en_equiv: How much is the meal fee?

explain_en: It is the money paid for group meals such as school lunch. It often appears in school notices and letters to parents, and is separate from household food expenses.

examples.ko: 엄마는 제가 용돈 달라고 하면 돈타령 그만하래요.
examples.en: Mom tells me to stop harping on about money whenever I ask for allowance.

examples.ko: 아침부터 무슨 돈타령이에요?
examples.en: Why are you going on about money since the morning?

examples.ko: 남편이 맨날 돈타령만 해서 지쳤어요.
examples.en: I'm worn out because my husband talks only about money every day.

examples.ko: 친구가 취업 전엔 돈타령을 안 했는데 변했어요.
examples.en: My friend never went on about money before getting a job, but he's changed.

examples.ko: 돈타령은 그만하고 일부터 해요.
examples.en: Stop talking about money and get to work first.

examples.ko: 누구나 월급날 전에는 돈타령이 나와요.
examples.en: Everybody starts complaining about money before payday.

explain: 돈이 없다, 돈이 필요하다는 말을 계속 되풀이하는 모습을 가리켜요. 듣는 사람이 질린다는 불평하는 말투로 쓰고, '돈타령을 하다', '돈타령이다' 형태로 말해요. 다른 말에도 '~타령'을 붙여서 같은 느낌으로 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My younger brother has been going on about money for days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돈타령'이 '하다'와 함께 쓰여 돈 이야기를 되풀이하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '돈타령' with '하다' describes repeatedly talking about money.

phrases.en: Money talk again? You said it last week too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 말이 돈 이야기뿐이라고 가볍게 불평할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to lightly complain that someone only talks about money.

phrases.en: My son has been asking for allowance money since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~타령'을 붙여서 한 가지를 계속 말하는 느낌을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '~타령' gives the feel of repeating one thing over and over.

explain_en: It describes someone repeating over and over that they have no money or need money. It is said in a tone of being fed up, as '돈타령을 하다' or '돈타령이다'. You can attach '타령' to other words for the same feeling.

examples.ko: 싸게 샀다고 해서 꼭 득은 아니에요.
examples.en: Buying something cheap isn't always a gain.

examples.ko: 그렇게 계속 싸우면 서로에게 득이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you keep fighting like that, neither of you gains anything.

examples.ko: 이번 거래는 손해도 득도 없었어요.
examples.en: This deal had neither loss nor gain.

examples.ko: 득과 실을 잘 따져 보고 결정하세요.
examples.en: Weigh the pros and cons carefully before you decide.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 득을 본 사람이 도대체 누구예요?
examples.en: Who on earth benefited from this?

examples.ko: 일찍 준비해 두면 나중에 우리 모두에게 득이 될 거예요.
examples.en: If we prepare early, it will benefit all of us later.

explain: '득'은 혼자보다 '득이 되다', '득을 보다', '득과 실'처럼 정해진 틀로 많이 나와요. 말할 때는 '이득'이 더 흔하고, 반대말은 '실'이나 '손해'예요.

phrases.example: 이 경험은 나중에 득이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: This experience will be a benefit later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 나에게 이로울 때 쓰는 대표적인 틀이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard pattern for something that works to your advantage.

phrases.en: I benefited thanks to that shop.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have gained an advantage.

phrases.example: 결정하기 전에 득과 실을 잘 따져 보세요.
phrases.en: Weigh the pros and cons before you decide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '실'과 함께 이익과 손해를 같이 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with its opposite 실 to mean gains and losses together.

explain_en: 득 rarely stands alone. It appears in fixed patterns such as 득이 되다, 득을 보다 and 득과 실. In speech 이득 is more common, and the opposites are 실 and 손해.

examples.ko: 친구가 빌린 돈을 떼먹고 연락이 끊겼어요.
examples.en: My friend skipped out on the money he borrowed and cut off contact.

examples.ko: 월급을 떼먹는 사장님 때문에 정말 힘들었어요.
examples.en: I had a really hard time because of a boss who withheld wages.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 내 돈을 떼먹을 사람이 아니에요.
examples.en: He's not the kind of person who would stiff me.

examples.ko: 회비를 떼먹은 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who ran off with the membership fees?

examples.ko: 빌린 돈을 자꾸 떼먹으면 신용을 잃어요.
examples.en: If you keep not paying back borrowed money, you lose people's trust.

examples.ko: 친구 돈을 떼먹지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't cheat your friend out of his money.

explain: 갚아야 할 돈이나 줄 돈을 일부러 안 주는 느낌의 구어체예요. 돈을 못 받은 쪽은 '떼이다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: If you don't repay borrowed money, you lose people's trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갚아야 할 돈을 일부러 안 주는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for deliberately not paying money owed.
phrases.en_equiv: to skip out on a debt

phrases.en: He ran off without paying his tab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 안 주고 달아나는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone flees without paying.

phrases.example: 내 돈 떼먹지 말고 이번 주에 꼭 갚아 줘요.
phrases.en: Don't stiff me; please pay me back this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떼먹지 말고'처럼 친한 사이에서 농담 반 경고로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: As in '떼먹지 말고', it can be a half-joking warning between close friends.

explain_en: It is a colloquial word with a feel of deliberately not paying money you owe. The person who didn't get paid says '떼이다'.

en: a whole lot; in great quantity

examples.ko: 세일이라서 옷을 왕창 샀어요.
examples.en: It was a sale, so I bought a whole lot of clothes.

examples.ko: 어제 비가 왕창 와서 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained heavily yesterday, so the roads were jammed.

examples.ko: 엄마가 김치를 왕창 담그셨어요.
examples.en: Mom made a huge amount of kimchi.

examples.ko: 월급날에 친구들에게 밥을 왕창 쐈어요.
examples.en: On payday, I treated my friends to a big meal.

examples.ko: 오늘 손님이 왕창 와서 정신이 없었어요.
examples.en: A whole bunch of customers came today, and it was hectic.

examples.ko: 주식이 왕창 올라서 기분이 좋아요!
examples.en: My stocks shot up a lot, so I'm in a good mood!

explain: '많이'보다 한꺼번에 확 많은 양이 생기거나 쓰일 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. '사다', '먹다', '오다', '쓰다'처럼 한 번에 많이 하는 동작과 잘 어울려요. 격식 있는 글에는 '매우 많이'를 써요.

phrases.en: I was hungry, so I ate a whole lot of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 아주 많이 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when eating a huge amount at once.

phrases.en: I spent a whole lot of money this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 한꺼번에 많이 나갔다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of a lot of money going out at once.

phrases.en: I bought a huge amount at the market.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 왕창, but with less of a sense of all at once.

explain_en: Compared with 많이, this casual word suggests a large amount arriving or being used all at once. It fits actions done in bulk, like 사다, 먹다, 오다 and 쓰다. In formal writing, use 매우 많이 instead.
